messages:
Sam W.: quick follow-up from the RFC: we need a clear fallback grace policy for midstream failures. do we let edge stream partial progress to clients or always cut and retry?
Kim L.: leaning toward streaming partial progress + a short grace window so UX doesn't regress. but that complicates billing + idempotency.
Jordan R.: agree on partialness; proposal: annotate responses with a `replay-token` trailer when we cut, so clients can resume without re-executing side effects.
Lia P.: +1 on token, but how long do we keep server-side state? storage and memory cost could explode if grace window is long.
Kim L.: thinking: 5s hard window for in-memory fast tokens, 5m soft window backed by cheap KV with eviction. beyond that, reject resume with 412.
Sam W.: that splits the cost. 5s handles most transient network flaps, 5m covers brief upstream work migrations. but what about retry budgets and canary tiers?
Jordan R.: tie token eligibility to retry budget + idempotency metadata. only idempotent requests (or explicitly resumable ops) get tokens. non-idempotent requests must use side-effect-safe endpoints or fall back to A/B route.
Lia P.: for billing: if we serve partial payloads, we must reflect consumed tokens in logs and show cost clarifications in console. otherwise customers will be surprised.
Kim L.: agreed. console should mark resumed calls and show pre/post token counts. trace id should include `resume=true` tag.
Sam W.: what about client-visible semantics? clients should see a deterministic trailer if resume possible, and a short `X-Resume-Expires` header.
Jordan R.: proto sketch: trailers: `resume-token: base64(...)`, `resume-expires-ms: 5000`, `resume-backed-by: mem|kv`. server returns `206` for partial with resume trailer, or `502`/`504` without resume.
Lia P.: careful with HTTP semantics — 206 implies range; maybe use `202 Accepted (partial)` with an explicit body envelope. but ok if we document in SDKs.
Sam W.: let's pick numeric codes later. more important: observability. we need a metric `edge.resume.attempts`, `edge.resume.success`, `edge.resume.evicted`.
Kim L.: also `edge.resume.cost-split` to allocate token/compute charge between original attempt and resume. product needs that for billing.
Jordan R.: implementation note: don't change existing stream shape. emit a thin envelope header/trailer so older clients ignore it. SDKs can opt-in to resume handling.
Lia P.: security: tokens must be HMACed with short TTL, bound to tenant and request-id. otherwise resume tokens can be replayed across tenants.
Sam W.: good catch. add `resume-hmac-v` header/versioning for future key rotation.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: edge/streaming-resume v1 -> staging at 2026-03-23 15:14 UTC :rocket:
Kim L.: action items: 1) finalize time windows (5s/5m) 2) proto trailer fields 3) metrics + billing hooks 4) SDK opt-in behavior 5) HMAC spec.
Sam W.: I'll spin a short RFC addendum with the proto and security stubs. want reviewers: @Kim L., @Jordan R., @Lia P. please review by EOD Friday.
Jordan R.: will do. quick comment: consider a conservative default of `resume=false` on hosted tier to reduce state churn for low-tier customers.
Lia P.: yep, and admin toggles per-tenant for Private deployments.
Sam W.: perfect. closing thread for now, will ping once addendum posted. :thumbsup:
